name: GPT-Live 1
access: ChatGPT Voice (default voice model on paid plans)

voice.input_audio: WebSocket: PCM 16-bit mono at 24 kHz (default) or 16 kHz, G.711 mu-law at 8 kHz, or G.711 A-law at 8 kHz, one format for input and output, fixed at session start; WebRTC and SIP negotiate the format; typed text is also accepted; no image or video [openai-guide-websockets] [openai-model-gpt-live-1]
voice.output_audio: The same format as the input on a WebSocket, a media track on WebRTC; a sideband connection receives copies as PCM 16-bit mono at 24 kHz [openai-guide-websockets] [openai-guide-server-controls]
voice.voices: 32 built-in voice names in the API schema, with marin as the default: the ten Realtime voices, the 12 named GPT-Live voices (quartz, ripple, vesper, willow, stone, gleam, meridian, bossa, tempo, beacon, delta, cinder), and ten that the guides do not describe (aube, brise, flitz, harema, juni, nira, noeul, nuri, shitan, sillage); custom voices for authorised customers [openai-ref-live-create] [openai-guide-live-sessions] [community-live-1]
voice.turn_detection: None to configure in the guides read: the model decides continuously when to listen, speak, pause or yield, and the guides expose no VAD or end-of-turn setting; the launch note lists explicit turn detection among production features without describing a setting [openai-guide-websockets] [community-live-1]
voice.interruption: Yes, native to full duplex: the model stops its answer when the user speaks and can make short listening sounds while the user talks; backend work keeps running after an interruption; microphone input can be muted; an appended instruction can also interrupt speech [openai-guide-live-prompting] [openai-guide-live-delegation] [openai-guide-live-sessions]
voice.latency: OpenAI: 0.798 s turn-taking latency, against 1.41 s for GPT-Realtime-2.1 [community-live-1]. Artificial Analysis time to first audio on Big Bench Audio: 1.34 s with an Astra backend at medium effort and 1.24 s with a Sol backend at low effort [aa-speech-to-speech]

pricing_usd_per_mtok.notes: $0.05 per minute of voice session, billed per second without rounding up; a WebRTC session creation bills 15 seconds up front, credited against the running duration; backend model and tool usage is billed separately at their own rates
